description:
Change a project of the current workspace: its name, kind, status, dates, amount and currency, the project it nests under, for a project how its work is priced (billing_method), for a campaign its channel (google_ads, linkedin_ads, reddit_ads, chatgpt_ads), objective (awareness, traffic, engagement, leads, sales), included and excluded audiences, for a flow its trigger audience, for a pipeline stage its win chance (probability), and for a deal its stage, owner, counterparty, win probability and position.

Use this tool when the user asks to rename a project, move it to another status (for example mark a deal won or lost), move a deal to another stage, change its dates, amount, owner, counterparty or chance, set how a project is billed, set a stage's win chance, or nest it under another project. Find the project_id first with a one-row well_query_records lookup.

REQUIRED: project_id.
OPTIONAL (only the fields the user wants changed): hidden, name, kind, status, start_date, end_date (YYYY-MM-DD), amount (a decimal string; the resulting project needs a currency), currency, parent_project_id, stage_project_id, owner_person_id, counterparty_company_id, counterparty_person_id, probability (a percentage from 0 through 100, at most two decimals; on a deal its own chance, on a pipeline stage the chance its open deals count at), position (a whole number from 0), billing_method (a project only: project_rate, service_rate, person_rate, fixed_fee, non_billable), channel and objective (a campaign only), included_audience_project_id and excluded_audience_project_id (a campaign only), trigger_audience_project_id (a flow only). Audience ids must name live audiences of this workspace. The ids are ids of this workspace. Use one-row well_query_records lookups to resolve them. Pass null to clear an optional field; an explicit null is a complete change.

Each kind takes its own parent, statuses and fields:
deal: no parent; status draft, active, paused, won, lost, archived; takes owner_person_id, counterparty_company_id, counterparty_person_id, stage_project_id, probability, position, end_date, amount, currency.
pipeline: no parent; status active, archived; takes no other field.
pipeline_stage: nests under a pipeline; status active, archived; takes position, probability.
cost_center: may nest under a cost_center; status active, archived; takes no other field.
property: no parent; status active, archived; takes no other field.
project: may nest under a project; status draft, active, paused, completed, archived; takes counterparty_company_id, counterparty_person_id, start_date, end_date, amount, currency, billing_method.
campaign: no parent; status draft, active, paused, completed, archived; takes start_date, end_date, channel, objective, included_audience_project_id, excluded_audience_project_id.
audience: no parent; status draft, active, paused, completed, archived; takes start_date, end_date.
flow: no parent; status draft, active, paused, completed, archived; takes start_date, end_date, trigger_audience_project_id.
ad: may nest under a campaign; status draft, active, paused, completed, archived; takes start_date, end_date.
A status moves along the kind's own path: a deal opens from draft, closes won or lost from active or paused, and a closed deal reopens to active before anything else; an archived project reopens to active. A field the kind does not take, or a move it does not allow, fails and nothing is written.

A pipeline stage's win chance is a workspace-wide setting: only an owner or an admin of the workspace can set or clear it, and it changes for the whole workspace. On WhatsApp, a complete typed order from an owner or an admin that names the stage and the new percent saves at once, and the reply says "Saved: <stage> now counts at <percent>% for the whole workspace." Any other stage order asks for one confirm first, and the confirm card names the workspace, the stage and the old and new percent.

A project a connected tool synced in (synced: true) keeps name, kind, parent_project_id, amount, currency, end_date, stage_project_id, owner_person_id, counterparty_company_id, counterparty_person_id, channel, objective, included_audience_project_id, excluded_audience_project_id, trigger_audience_project_id from that tool: a change that names any of them fails, even beside others, and the user changes them in that tool. status, probability, position, start_date, billing_method, hidden change in Well on a synced project too. A patch is complete when it names the fields to change; do not ask for fields it leaves alone. On WhatsApp, the person's complete typed change approves and writes at once, except a stage's win chance, which saves at once only in the complete typed order above. Other surfaces still use their normal approval.

hidden: true hides the project from Well's lists and figures and keeps it; hidden: false shows it again. It works on a synced project too, since no sync writes it. When the person asks to delete a synced project, well_delete_project refuses and offers this hide: ask the person, then call this tool with only project_id and hidden: true.

Returns { success: true, project } on success, or { success: false, error } on failure.

billing_method.description: How the work of a project is priced: project_rate, service_rate, person_rate, fixed_fee, non_billable. Only a project takes it; null clears it.

channel.description: The ad platform a campaign runs on: google_ads, linkedin_ads, reddit_ads, chatgpt_ads. Only a campaign takes it; null clears it.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

hidden.description: true hides the row from Well's lists and figures and keeps it, with every value a connected tool wrote; false shows it again. Omit to leave it as it is.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A retried write with the same key returns the original result instead of re-applying the operation.

kind.description: What the project is: deal, pipeline, pipeline_stage, cost_center, property, project, campaign, audience, flow, ad. Ask the user when it is not clear.

objective.description: The campaign objective: awareness, traffic, engagement, leads, sales. Only a campaign takes it; null clears it.

project_id.description: The project to change, from a one-row well_query_records lookup.

status.description: Where the project stands: draft, active, paused, won, lost, archived, completed. A kind holds only some of them. Ask the user when it is not clear.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several — a write lands in exactly one workspace and this call would not say which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_update_project

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.
